summary: Describes the standardization collaboration between 3GPP2, a mobile phone standards group, and the IETF, and how they coordinate work.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3131 describes how two standards bodies, 3GPP2 and the IETF, work together on specifications for mobile networks. It explains where each group's drafts are published, how they tell each other about problems, and who the contact points are on each side.

questions: how does the ietf work with 3gpp2
what is the 3gpp2 liaison in the iesg
how do 3gpp2 and the ietf work together
subtitle: How a mobile network standards body and the IETF arrange to write specifications that fit together

tldr.problem: Mobile network specifications and Internet specifications were written by separate bodies, so a device or network that relies on both could end up with two incompatible descriptions of the same thing.
tldr.mechanism: The memo sets out principles for the two bodies to work together: 3GPP2 uses Internet standards unchanged where it can and sends the cases that need changes to the IETF working groups, while named contact points in each organisation handle documents, discussions and administrative questions.
tldr.outcome: It describes a working arrangement rather than a protocol: an IETF rapporteur inside 3GPP2 and a 3GPP2 liaison inside the Internet Engineering Steering Group, with each organisation keeping its own rules on intellectual property, approval and maintenance.

facts.label: 3GPP2 technical groups named
facts.value: 5: TSG-A, TSG-C, TSG-N, TSG-P and TSG-S

facts.label: Contact roles in the arrangement
facts.value: 2: an IETF rapporteur and a 3GPP2 liaison

today: RFC 3131 is an Informational memo from June 2001 that has not been obsoleted or updated. It records a working arrangement between two standards bodies rather than a protocol, and it notes that this kind of non-protocol document does not directly affect the security of the Internet.

sections.title: Purpose and Ground Rules
sections.content:
This memo sets out a set of principles and guidelines that serves as the basis for collaboration between 3GPP2 and the IETF. 3GPP2, the Third Generation Partnership Project 2, is the body that writes specifications for CDMA2000 mobile networks. The IETF, the Internet Engineering Task Force, writes the protocols the Internet runs on.

The stated objective is securing the timely development of technical specifications that facilitate maximum interoperability with existing fixed and mobile Internet systems, devices and protocols. Underneath that, each organisation operates according to its own rules and procedures, including rules governing intellectual property rights, specification elaboration, approval and maintenance. The memo notes that it uses terminology specialised to IETF or 3GPP2, and points to an appendix for the acronyms.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo sets out how a mobile network standards body and the IETF cooperate on specifications. Each side keeps its own rules for approving and maintaining documents, and the aim is that a phone and the Internet protocols it uses fit together.

sections.title: Why the Two Groups Collaborate
sections.content:
The preferred 3GPP2 approach is to use the Internet standards unchanged, if feasible, and 3GPP2 has no intention of duplicating work already performed in the IETF. What it does need is a way to raise the cases where an IETF specification has to be added to, or modified, to fulfil 3GPP2's needs. In such cases 3GPP2 takes its concerns directly to the appropriate IETF working group for resolution, or to an appropriate Area Director if no suitable working group can be found.

The interest runs the other way as well. The IETF needs the wireless expertise that sits inside 3GPP2, and 3GPP2 organises its technical work into Technical Specification Groups. TSG-A and TSG-C are responsible for the radio access networks based on CDMA, and with them the characteristics of the physical transport. TSG-N is responsible for mobility management and the other core network protocols and functionalities. TSG-P is responsible for data services and applications. TSG-S is responsible for the service and system aspects, including the overall architecture, security and operation and maintenance.
sections.plainLanguage: 3GPP2 wants to use the IETF's protocols as they stand, and sends any change it needs straight to the relevant IETF working group. In return, the IETF gets access to 3GPP2's knowledge of radio networks, which is organised into five technical groups.

sections.title: Sharing Documents and Talking
sections.content:
Both bodies encourage the sharing of draft documents that are of mutual interest. The 3GPP2 working documents are available on its web site, grouped according to the meeting, and they are also on an FTP server that is open to anyone. 3GPP2 specifications, those that have completed the 15-day Steering Committee review, are published on the web site as well. IETF documents, including the preliminary working documents known as Internet-Drafts, are available on the IETF web site and on various shadow sites. Either side can learn the structure of the other's documents and web site by contacting the contact points named for that purpose.

Informal communication at working level is encouraged wherever possible. The vast majority of technical discussion and decision making at the IETF is done over mailing lists, and interested individuals are recommended to subscribe to and take part in them. The 3GPP2 mailing lists, however, are not open to the general public, so work of mutual interest is discussed on the relevant IETF mailing lists instead. When it is deemed necessary, formal communication between the two bodies is permitted as well, and the relevant IETF Area Directors and 3GPP2 technical leadership are encouraged and authorised to facilitate it.
sections.plainLanguage: Drafts from both sides are published openly, and most discussion happens on IETF mailing lists, which anyone can join. The 3GPP2 lists are closed, so shared work is argued about in the open lists instead.

sections.title: The Two Contact Points
sections.content:
Two named roles carry the collaboration. Inside 3GPP2, an IETF rapporteur function is established in the 3GPP2 Steering Committee. Whoever is appointed to it is the initial contact point in 3GPP2 for matters pertaining to the cooperation between the two bodies, and works with the concerned working groups and TSGs to support the interaction. The chairman of the Steering Committee can always be contacted as well.

Inside the IETF, the memo proposes the appointment of a specific person in the Internet Engineering Steering Group to act as a 3GPP2 liaison. The preferred way for an organisation to work with the IETF is through the working groups, and the IETF has a limited number of liaison relationships with other organisations, appointing a person only when the conditions warrant it. The liaison acts as the initial contact point in the IETF for the administrative aspects of the collaboration that cannot easily be handled in other ways, such as questions that working groups and Area Directors cannot settle at a technical level. The role does not carry the expectation of attendance at 3GPP2 meetings or participation in 3GPP2 administrative processes, all of the liaison's work is expected to be carried out by electronic mail, and the liaison will not have the ability to make exceptions to, or special provisions for, IETF policies and procedures.
sections.plainLanguage: One person on each side is the named contact: an IETF rapporteur inside the 3GPP2 Steering Committee, and a 3GPP2 liaison inside the IETF's steering group. The liaison handles paperwork rather than technical arguments, and cannot bend IETF rules.

sections.title: Who Can Take Part
sections.content:
To assist the flow of information between the organisations, the IETF can, on a per case basis, appoint an observer to participate in and represent the IETF at 3GPP2 technical meetings. IETF meetings are open to any interested individuals.

3GPP2 partners, which the memo abbreviates as OPs and MRPs, or individual members can participate in any of the IETF meetings in accordance with the existing IETF procedures. 3GPP2 meetings are also open to any interested individual, but such individuals do not have voting privileges there. The meeting schedule can be found on the 3GPP2 web site.
sections.plainLanguage: Anyone may attend an IETF meeting, and any individual may sit in on a 3GPP2 meeting, though only 3GPP2 members vote there. The IETF may also send an observer to a 3GPP2 technical meeting when it helps.
